title: Sell Mineral Rights in Bergholz, OH
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Bergholz, OH | Jefferson County
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Bergholz, Jefferson County? See how spacing units and pooled acreage work before you sell, plus get a straightforward cash offer.
heroLead: Bergholz sits in southern Jefferson County, ground that's been folded into horizontal spacing units alongside neighboring Harrison County acreage.
intro: If you own minerals near Bergholz, there's a decent chance your tract has been pooled into a spacing unit that crosses into Harrison County, since operators lay out horizontal units by geology and lease position, not county lines. Understanding how pooling works helps explain why your royalty check, if you're getting one, might reference a well that isn't physically under your own tract.
That's normal, and it's worth understanding rather than being confused by, since it's central to how modern shale development actually works across this part of eastern Ohio.

sections.heading: How pooling and spacing units work
paragraphs: A horizontal Utica well might run a mile or more, crossing under dozens of separate tracts and multiple property owners along the way. Rather than drilling a well per tract, operators combine, or pool, all the mineral interests within the unit's boundary and pay each owner their proportional share of production based on how much of the unit their acreage represents.

That's why your division order lists a decimal interest rather than a flat share, it reflects your tract's percentage of the total pooled unit, which could span acreage well beyond what your family actually owns.

sections.heading: What this means for a Bergholz-area sale
paragraphs: If your minerals are part of an active pooled unit, your division order and royalty statements are the clearest way to establish value, they show your exact decimal interest and recent production. If your tract sits outside any current unit boundary, an offer is based more on likely future development, informed by activity in adjoining units nearby.

sections.heading: Confirming ownership before you sell
paragraphs: Jefferson County deed and lease records are held at the recorder's office in Steubenville. Because so much of Bergholz-area land is held in long-standing family tracts, confirming your exact share, whether you own it outright or split it with relatives, is a necessary first step before any serious offer can be made.

faqs.question: Why does my royalty check reference a well I've never heard of?
faqs.answer: Horizontal wells often extend under multiple tracts through pooling, so your interest can be tied to a well physically located some distance from your own property while still being under your unit.

faqs.question: What if my tract isn't in any current spacing unit?
faqs.answer: It can still be sold, the offer will just be based on comparable activity nearby rather than an existing production record.

faqs.question: How do I find out which unit my minerals are pooled into?
faqs.answer: Your division order will list the unit name, or the Ohio Department of Natural Resources' well database can be searched by township to identify nearby active units.
